paragraphs: Wavetronix makes radar sensors that detect the presence of vehicles at the stop bar. The buyers are traffic agencies, and the collected data can be shared among several of them. That data feeds uses such as trip times and congestion alerts.

One system is a multi-approach stop bar detector designed for smaller intersections. It covers four approaches of three lanes or less per approach. The flagship stop bar detector sees both moving and stopped vehicles. A safety product tracks vehicles in the dilemma zone out to 600 feet. An extended range version protects large trucks and buses out to 900 feet. A cabinet device supplies power and communication for two to six sensors. A newer add-on analyzes split failures and turning movement counts and recommends updated max green times.

The company says it opened in 2000. All sensors are made at its headquarters in Springville, Utah. It states that it supports and complies with the Build America Buy America Act. It also says it is driven to succeed for customers, not for investors or shareholders.
